I moved to Wrexham from south Wales so I registered at Bryn Darland as it's my local surgery.

The consultant who I was under in south Wales wrote to Bryn Darland and myself explaining that, because I had moved from their catchment area, I was discharged from their care. However, I should make an appointment with my new GP (Bryn Darland) to request further tests as there were slight abnormalities. Pretty simple to understand I'd say. Firstly, Bryn Darland suggested they hadn't received such letter. I thought to myself 'fair enough' even though I'm sure they're probably available digitally on my records. Took them the letter which they took a copy of and got told to wait for someone to get in touch. I did just this only for someone from the surgery to then message me asking when I'd moved away from Wrexham. I mean, come on??

I have a repeat prescription which they asked for a copy of when I signed up. I got told that because I had moved, it would take time (around a month) for my records to arrive from my previous GP. Again, fair enough. I checked the app after around 8 weeks and only one item was listed. I contacted them asking where the other items were, only to be asked 'what other items? We weren't aware of anything else?' Why take a copy of my prescription in the first place then? And again, surely it's all digitally available, too?

I've been waiting for blood tests as instructed by my previous consultant  only to have my appointment cancelled twice because of 'staff sickness'. I mean, it would take someone all of 5 minutes to draw blood but I've been waiting since the middle of the year and cancelled for weeks at a time. The receptionist even got a bit defensive because I started to become a little frustrated. In fairness, she did give me an alternative option to see if there was availability, but having checked, their appointments didn't suit because I had already made plans around the previous appointments you keep making and cancelling.

I know mistakes happen and staff get sick, but look at it from my perspective. I think you need to sharpen up a touch.

I did see one of the doctors once, though.
